plot: Tuesday morning in the backyard Crispy confronts Mr. Pot, the old black petunia pot with three dents that the 1976 newspaper blamed for the bakery fire, and Mr. Pot grumpily admits he was on the stove while snapping 'don't say Walter's name' before anyone did; Mom plans to put him on her new bakery's stove, Bup's push to hide him fails, angry Lolly tips him over (Bup comes up as a 'chocolate flower cake'), and Crispy reads the twist scratched on the bottom — 'My fault, not yours. Forgive me. W.': Walter fell asleep with the stove on and Mr. Pot let the town blame him for fifty years to protect the baker; Crispy forgives him, becomes the bakery's night guard, and Mia runs out — someone just ordered five hundred rolls before the bakery even opens.

beats.say: There you are. Three dents. Like three eyes. It was you!
Fifty years I hid in the dark. Now you answer me!
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Tuesday morning. The backyard. Cold dew on every leaf.
In the corner sits an old black pot full of petunias.
Fifty years, little cinder. You sure took your time.
Crispy, easy! We came to ask questions. Not to start a war.
He was on that stove. The newspaper says so.
Three round dents. A ninety-nine percent match.
Ninety-nine? Ha! Make it a hundred, little triangle.
Excuse me, sir. You burned our friend, and you laugh?
Don't. Say Walter's name, and this talk is over.
W-wait. Nobody said Walter. Why did he say Walter?
And why does he sit so c-crooked? Like he's hiding his bottom?
Pim, sweetie. Nobody wants to look at a pot's bottom.
The back door bangs open. Mom walks out in yellow gloves.
Mom says the old pot goes to her bakery. Onto the stove.
No. Not again. Not Mom's bakery. Not her dream.
Mom goes back inside for a bucket. She scrubs him after lunch.
Team, if that bakery burns, Mom loses everything.
Then he never leaves this garden. I'll stop him myself.
Crispy's ember eyes glow hotter and hotter. The petunias droop.
Bup jumps between them. New plan. Roll the pot behind the shed.
Push, team! On three! One, two... ugh! He weighs a ton!
Lolly's sweet smile disappears. Her icing drips start to shake.
Nobody. Laughs. At. My. Friends.
One tiny star. One huge shove. The old pot tips over.
Soil pours out. Right on top of Bup.
Bup pops up. Brown all over. A pink petunia on his head.
Bup! You're a chocolate cake! With a flower on top!
I'm a loaf! A dirty, flowery loaf! Nobody eat me!
But Crispy isn't laughing. He rolls to the bottom of the pot.
Put me back! Don't read that! That's private!
It's scratched in the metal. It says: Old friend.
My fault, not yours. Forgive me. W.
W. Walter. Walter scratched that? For you?
Mr. Pot is quiet. For the first time. No laugh. No steam.
Walter fell asleep in his chair. Stove on. Me on top.
I boiled dry. I rattled my lid. Nobody woke up.
The paper blamed a pot. Not a sweet old baker. Fine.
You let the whole town hate you? For fifty years?
The town loved its baker. Walter loved his town. Easy choice.
So all that grumpy fry-you talk was just an act?
A grumpy pot is easier to be than a sorry one.
Crispy's eyes cool down. Slowly. From red to soft orange.
I hid in the dark. You hid in petunias. Same thing.
Then Mom comes back. Bucket. Gloves. Scrub brush.
H-he's going on a stove! What if it happens again?
It won't. Not if somebody watches that stove every night.
Somebody who glows in the dark. And never sleeps.
Mom lifts the pot. Under it, she finds Walter's words.
Then Mia runs out, waving Mom's phone.
The bakery isn't open yet. Someone just ordered five hundred rolls.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
